## Design

### 2026-11-01: INTRO

**4h**

INTRO

Welcome to this journal about my display project "Peekboard". Why the name you ask ? First of all its a peak project XD and on top of that I want to peek at it to see some information.

PROJECT

The idea itself is a display or monitor that I can place below my other monitors and have a dashboard of a variety of infos and cool little things. Its powered by usb c and also gets data over this line.

TABLE OF CONTENTS

- rough idea, dimensions and layout
- rough parts
- first feature ideas

- complete parts list and layout
- complete pin mapout (on paper first)
- complete feature planout

IDEAS LAYOUT AND DIMENSIONS

I started with deciding on an idea and settled with a small dashboard for my setup. I drew the Dimensions how i would like them and coincedentaly the dimensions fit nearly perfect with a 4" TFT SCREEN. Then I added some tactiles and a rotary encoder to the side and cooked up a backstand design for the whole thing.
![IMG_3418](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/wKsIODyJMOqccfQq70tFSoimsjj2E03H/e6125c3cd02d369a94374f60451bcee427e10e3cefa6b9e86d19407491f8bbea.jpg)
Here you can see my notes on this as well as some todo scribbles.

ROUGH PARTS

At this stage I only settled with some barebones parts.
The ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 as brain because it has decent RAM, which I need for video buffers for the camera feature.

The switches and encoder where also strait forward. I just used what i was familiar with from the earlier projects.

I also did add some SK6812 LEDs because they come in a badge of 20pcs. And I already bought some for another project. So my stock comes in handy now XD.

EARLY FEATURES

At first I only had in mind to display some statistics and use it as a camera monitor. Later came some more features, but I did some research for the cam setup and settled with a relay system over my PC.

PARTS LIST AND LAYOUT

After all primary work was done I resumed with noting all schematic circuits down. This took me two pages of writing which was relatively few compared to my previous project.
